title: Lightning Is 5x Hotter Than the Sun, and Thunder Is the Air Exploding

parts.text: A lightning bolt is five times hotter
parts.tts: A lightning bolt is five times hotter,

parts.text: than the surface of the Sun.
Yet the channel it burns through the air
parts.tts: Yet the channel it burns through the air,

parts.text: is barely wider than your thumb.
that thin thread of air hits twenty-eight thousand degrees Celsius.
Air that hot cannot stay still.
Count the seconds until you hear it.
Every three seconds is about one kilometer.

sources: Temperature: lightning heats the air around its channel to as much as 50,000 F (about 28,000 C), five times the Sun's surface. US National Weather Service, weather.gov/mlb/what_is_lightning.
Thunder: energy from the channel heats the air briefly to around 50,000 F, which causes the air to explode outward. NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/lightning.
Channel width: the actual diameter of a lightning channel is one to two inches (about 2.5 to 5 cm). NOAA NSSL Severe Weather 101, lightning types. The script says 'barely wider than your thumb'.
Distance rule: thunder takes about five seconds to travel a mile, which is about three seconds per kilometre (speed of sound about 343 m/s). NWS lightning safety guidance.
